sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and logging
sections.what: Loads the input and logging tools and creates a logger so warnings show up in the service logs.
sections.why: Lets the module report problems without stopping the whole service.

sections.name: ImagePreprocessor (part 1)
sections.title: Entry point and image cleanup
sections.what: Chooses the path for the file. PDFs are returned unchanged. Images are opened, transparency is flattened to white, converted to grey, and contrast is stretched.
sections.why: Makes dark, transparent, or coloured scans easier for the text reader to see.
sections.watch_out: PDFs are not converted, so PDF uploads reach OCR unchanged.

sections.name: ImagePreprocessor (part 2)
sections.title: Enlarging and saving the result
sections.what: Enlarges small images, saves the result as a 300 DPI PNG, and falls back to the original bytes if anything fails.
sections.why: The code comments say the text reader needs letters around 30 pixels tall, and very small dots can be filtered out as noise.
sections.watch_out: The 300 DPI value is only metadata and does not resample the pixels. Enlargement has no upper size limit.

summary: Prepares uploaded images so the OCR text reader can read them more accurately, by flattening transparency, converting to grey, stretching contrast, and enlarging small text.
purpose: Cleans an image before it is sent to OCR. PDF handling is listed as a plan but is not built yet.
why: Reason not stated in the code, but the comments say the OCR engine misses very small text, so images are enlarged and contrast is stretched.
how: The entry method checks the content type. PDFs are returned unchanged. Images are opened, transparent or palette areas are painted white, the image is converted to grey, contrast is stretched, small images are enlarged, and the result is saved as a PNG. Any error returns the original bytes.
inputs: Raw file bytes and a content type string such as image/png or application/pdf.
outputs: New PNG bytes ready for OCR, or the original bytes if processing fails.
risks: PDFs pass through unchanged, so later steps receive PDF data that the OCR step may not read. Enlarging has no size limit, so very large images can use a lot of memory. Steps named in the docstring, such as deskew, noise removal, binarization and auto-crop, are not in the code.
debug: If scans read poorly, first check whether the input was a PDF. If output looks identical to input, look in the logs for a fallback warning, which means processing failed and the raw bytes were returned.
